checks.tolerance: Hides source object key 622 (folder), exports the original scene and reimports it: the folder reads back hidden and the character inside it stays visible. The CharaStudio side of ST-T03 visibility (reloading the exported scene in the original player) is not covered here.

Renames source object key 622 (folder), exports the original scene and reimports it: the new name reads back. Camera and route renames are not exercised because the fixture scene contains neither object type; the character-name rejection half of ST-T03 rename is a StudioModel export guard covered by the Engine suite.

Edits face slot 20 on character key 0 and body slot 0 on character key 65, exports the original scene and reimports it: both rates read back within 1e-5. The inspector's live visual update and Reset to card are not covered (no headless pixel or reset assertion).

Edits the body.skinMainColor card color on character key 0, exports the original scene and reimports it: the edited rgba reads back on every component within 1e-5. The hair color edit is NOT part of this scenario: hair.parts.0.baseColor is a draft color on this card but binds no material on the imported assembly, so export skips the writeback; the live preview update and Reset to card stay unchecked.

Selects catalog clip [0,2,0] on character key 0 (saved clip [0,4,0]) with speed 1.5 and forceLoop on: the live animation state the preview plays matches the group/category/no exactly, speed within 1e-5, loop equal; after the original-scene export and reimport the new catalog IDs, speed and loop read back unchanged, and control character key 65 still reports its saved clip [0,0,2]. The clip actually plays on screen is not asserted (no pixel check).

Rotates FK bone 19 of character key 65 to [0,35,0] degrees (which also turns FK on): the document holds the exact degrees within 1e-5 and the left-hand guide (bone 21) sits further than 1e-5 from its pre-edit position. After export and reimport the guide lands within 0.02 of its post-edit position: export writes the degrees into the character's bone record, so after reimport the pose is asserted by bone position, not by the document's edit overlay (import never repopulates that overlay). IK mode and IK target edits stay unchecked.

Drives the REAL mouse handlers (mouseDown / eight mouseDragged / mouseUp, left button, no modifiers) over the GPU pick pass: the scenario projects bone 19's guide origin with the view camera, scans ±120 px for a pixel whose pick id is the z rotate ring (the z ring is the one open to this scene's view camera; y and x project nearly edge-on there), grabs it and drags 60,40 px. The drag must hold a non-zero FK rotation on bone 19 (the angle comes out of the ring geometry, so it is asserted non-zero, not equal to a number) and move the left-hand guide (bone 21) further than 1e-5 from its pre-drag position. Exactly one undo snapshot is pushed (by mouseDown), so one undo restores the hand within 1e-4; after redo, export and reimport the guide lands within 0.02 of its post-drag position. The drag degree readback and picked pixel id are recorded in the step detail. Before the drag, a hoverGizmo step drives the REAL mouseMoved hover (R7 phase 2, item 5), which picks asynchronously for the latest mouse position only: over the same z ring and an off-gizmo corner of the scan box, in three sequences of moves partly faster than a pick completes, each settled the way a click settles the hover first. on-off-on must highlight the z ring, off and on-off nothing (the ring's result arrives stale and is dropped); after each, the hovered axis must equal what the synchronous pick finds at the final position, and the frame the app built must draw exactly that ring (or no axis) in the highlight color. The six moves must coalesce three times, apply three results and drop at least two stale ones.

With IKKOKU_STUDIO_ITEM_CATALOG set, the import diagnostics must report `Items rendered from the converted catalog: 19; unmapped keys: none.`, and an export of all 19 placeholder items plus a reimport must still report that line. The rendered transforms and saved colors of the props (the visual half of ST-T04) are not asserted.

On scene-x (two active cameras, IKKOKU-A key 0 and IKKOKU-B key 2) the import must pick the last active camera in depth-first order (key 2) as the load winner; toggling camera 0 must make it active, and after export+reimport the written flags must make key 0 the winner again. This exercises our own load/export rule (ST-A06/ST-T03 active camera); reloading the exported scene in the original CharaStudio player is not covered.

On scene-x, toggling the active camera key 2 off must leave no active camera (orbit view); export writes every camera flag false and a reimport must still show no active camera. Deactivating key 0 (not the winner) is not scripted; the reload happens in our importer, not the original player.

Renames camera object key 0 on scene-x, exports the original scene and reimports it: the new name reads back on the camera placeholder (the camera-object half of ST-T03 rename, which the folder-only rename-folder scenario could not reach). The active-camera flags stay untouched by the rename; the winner (key 2) is not re-asserted here.

On the stt11c route scene (routes key 0 and key 3, both saved active) the inspector must report key 0 playing; toggling it must stop it, and after export+reimport key 0 must read back stopped (its flag written) while key 3 still reads back playing (its flag untouched). Only the play-state flag round trip is asserted; whether the character actually animates along the route is not observable headlessly.

ST-T11 route children: on the CharaStudio-authored scene-route-children.png (route key 0, saved playing and looping over four points; its children are folder key 9 and the fixture female key 10, which renders on the route) both children's world positions, read through the same placement walk refresh() renders with, move more than 0.5 m in a 2 s advance and the folder more than 0.1 m in the next 0.5 s; stopping the route pins both back to point 0 (within 1e-5 of their start) and they hold there through a further 2 s advance, and after export+reimport the route reads back stopped and both children still hold. Speed parity with the original tween, the Play all / Replay all / Stop all buttons and rendered pixels are not asserted.

R4/ST-A06 mirrored camera parent: on the CharaStudio-authored scene-mirrored-camera.png (camera IKKOKU-MIRROR key 2 under item key 0 with scale (-1, 1, 1), saved active; control camera IKKOKU-CONTROL key 3 under item key 1 with scale (1, 1, 1)) the load winner is camera 2, and through StudioModel.viewCamera the preview renders from exactly the saved scene camera while the status line reports 'Source camera "IKKOKU-MIRROR" (camera 2) view unresolved: Source camera object parent frame is mirrored' and the view indicator reads 'Saved camera shown: source camera "IKKOKU-MIRROR" (camera 2) has a mirrored parent', never 'Viewing through'; the tree labels read 'IKKOKU-MIRROR (camera 2)' and 'IKKOKU-CONTROL (camera 3)'; toggling camera 3 looks through it with the indicator 'Viewing through source camera "IKKOKU-CONTROL" (camera 3)' (view position within 1e-5 of its world placement and forward within 0.01 degrees, not the saved camera), toggling camera 2 back falls back again, and after export+reimport the same holds; deactivating camera 3 last leaves no active camera, the saved view, an empty indicator and the status 'Source camera "IKKOKU-CONTROL" (camera 3) deactivated; orbit controls restored.' The original player does look through the mirrored camera (scene-records.md 'Mirrored camera parent'); matching that pose, a mirror further up the chain and rendered pixels are not asserted.

ST-T03 acceptance export for the CharaStudio reload probe: on scene-x hide folder key 1, rename camera key 0 to IKKOKU-A2 and folder key 1 to IKKOKU-F2, export the original scene and reimport it; the hidden flag and both names must read back in our importer. The same PNG is loaded in the original CharaStudio by Tools/reverse/original_scene_reload_probe.py; see docs/reference/studio/scene-editing.md for the recorded CharaStudio result.

ST-T03 acceptance export for the CharaStudio reload probe: on scene-x the load winner is key 2; toggling camera key 0 active must make it the view camera, and after export+reimport our importer must still pick key 0. The same PNG is loaded in the original CharaStudio by Tools/reverse/original_scene_reload_probe.py, which records which camera the player's view uses; see docs/reference/studio/scene-editing.md.

ST-T03 acceptance export for the CharaStudio reload probe: on the stt11c route scene stop route key 0 (exported with key 3 still active), export and reimport; our importer must read key 0 stopped and key 3 playing. The same PNG is loaded in the original CharaStudio by Tools/reverse/original_scene_reload_probe.py, which records whether each route plays there; see docs/reference/studio/scene-editing.md.

ST-T03 acceptance export for the CharaStudio reload probe: on the stt11c route scene rename route key 3 to IKKOKU-R3 (export validation must accept the route name edit, and the play states must be untouched by it), export and reimport; the route stays playing in our importer, which reads the record name back as IKKOKU-R3 (since ST-T03g routes import under their saved names). The same PNG is loaded in the original CharaStudio by Tools/reverse/original_scene_reload_probe.py, which records the route name it reads back; see docs/reference/studio/scene-editing.md.

ST-T01 acceptance edit on the CharaStudio-authored scene scene-char.png (one female in the default pose, FK disabled; produced by Tools/reverse/original_scene_reload_probe.py --author-character from a synthetic fixture card): turn FK on and rotate bone 19 to [0,35,0] degrees, assert the exact degrees and the moved left-hand guide (bone 21), export and reimport; after reimport the guide reproduces its post-edit position within 0.02 (the scene's saved FK lives on the reimported preview, like studio-scenario-fk-edit; the degrees read back in the file itself are asserted by the reload probe), and the same export's saved bone-19 rotation is asserted against [0,35,0] by the original player. The same PNG is loaded in the original CharaStudio by Tools/reverse/original_scene_reload_probe.py, which records enableFK, the active FK groups, the bone's saved rotation and the hand world position it reads back; see docs/reference/studio/scene-editing.md.

On scene-x the two camera objects and the scene light must be live at load; renaming the folder placeholder (key 1) and undoing must keep the look-through winner (key 2), both camera entries and the scene light (before ST-T15 the undo emptied all of them), and redoing must re-apply the name. Toggling to camera key 0, exporting and reimporting must read back key 0 active: the export only rewrites the active flags because the load-winner record survived the undo. ST-T15/ST-T01 camera half.

The props scene's 19 converted item assets and the scene light must be live at load; hiding folder key 622 and undoing must restore it visible with all 19 item entries and the scene light still cached (before ST-T15 the undo emptied them), and redoing must hide it again. Export+reimport re-asserts the hidden folder and the 19-item diagnostic. ST-T15/ST-T01 props half; the rendered assets themselves are only censused, not pixel-checked.

The props scene imported WITHOUT IKKOKU_STUDIO_ITEM_CATALOG: no item resolves to a converted asset, so no item has a runtime cache entry, legitimately. Hiding folder key 622, undoing and redoing must never re-read the scene file (rehydrations stays 0): rehydration keys off the import's coverage, not off missing entries, so such scenes keep their live camera and route state across undo. Export+reimport re-asserts the hidden folder (a reimport is an import, so still no rehydration). Rendering is not checked.

On the stt11c route scene, stopping route key 0 and renaming key 3 then undoing must keep both route runtimes live (2 entries; before ST-T15 the undo dropped them), roll the key 3 name back, and keep the runtime play state: key 0 stays stopped because play state is runtime-only and never part of an undo snapshot. Export+reimport then reads key 0 back stopped (its flag written by the export) and key 3 playing. ST-T15/ST-T01 route half; whether the character animates along the route is not observable headlessly.

Saves the imported props scene natively (StudioModel.saveScene, a Studio document card under .local/) after hiding folder key 622; the 19 converted item entries and the scene light must still be live after the save (saving must not disturb the runtime), and the hidden folder must read back hidden. The reload half is the next, ordered check. ST-T01.

Loads the document the previous check saved, in a fresh process with NO IKKOKU_SOURCE_SCENE (the import never runs; the scenario's first step is loadDocument): folder key 622 must read back hidden and the 19 converted item entries and the scene light must be rehydrated from the original scene file the card names. Before ST-T01 a native load restored none of them. ST-T01.
Saves scene-x natively with the load-winner camera (key 2) live: both camera cache entries and the scene light must survive the save untouched. The reload half is the next, ordered check. ST-T01.

Loads the saved scene-x card in a fresh process with no import: both camera entries and the scene light must be rehydrated and the look-through camera must be key 2, the FILE's load winner — the live camera choice a user had before the save is runtime state the document never carried and deliberately does not come back. ST-T01.

Stops route key 0 on the stt11c route scene, then saves the document natively: both route entries and the scene light must survive, and the live play state must still report key 0 stopped (the save must not rewrite play state through the caches). The reload half is the next, ordered check. ST-T01.

Loads the saved route card in a fresh process with no import: both route runtimes and the scene light must be rehydrated and key 0 must report playing again, because play state restarts from the SAVED flag (true; the live stop before the save was runtime-only, exactly as after an undo keeps it). Whether the character animates along the route is not observable headlessly. ST-T01.

Character 65's TARGET eye look is live against the lane scene's camera; dragging the view left and right flips both iris-shift angle rates between the saturated (+1, +1) and (-1, -1) sides, raising and lowering it moves the vertical rate past +/-0.5, and the head and neck bone positions stay exactly still (no eye bones exist, so the eyes never move the skeleton). The state survives export and reimport. Iris texture pixels (EyeLookMaterialControll) stay unautomated.

Character 65's neck carries the FIX override ("FIX holds the saved neck rotation."): orbiting the camera across the scene never moves its head or neck bone. No TARGET/AWAY neck character exists in any scene under the fixture root, so the animated-neck half of ST-T07 neck look stays unautomated.

ST-T07 neck look TARGET/AWAY: on the CharaStudio-authored scene-neck-target.png, character 0 (neck pattern 1, TARGET) and character 147 (neck pattern 2, AWAY), both eyes pattern 1 (TARGET), get the live gaze runtime. The turn is measured on the front-hair root bone 100 (cf_J_hairF_00, a head child; a pure neck/head yaw leaves the head bone's own position unmoved) in each character's rig frame: orbiting the camera 60 degrees to one side moves the TARGET hair more than 0.05 and the AWAY hair more than 0.15, and the two end more than 0.15 apart (opposite sides); orbiting to the other side moves the TARGET hair more than 0.1 again while the AWAY hair returns within 0.01 of its front-camera pose and is again more than 0.15 from TARGET's. After export+reimport the gaze is live again and both poses reproduce within 0.01. Exact turn angles against the original are recorded in docs, not asserted; the FK-neck half of ST-T07 neck look stays unautomated.

Automatic blinking renders a closing within 7 s of the live clock, turning the Studio toggle off holds the eyes open for the next 7 s, turning it back on blinks again, and the card's saved hand-pattern pair reads back after export and reimport.

The converted hand-pattern library replays the card's saved [5, 6] pair: after 0.0667 s the left middle-finger bone has moved off its frame-0 position (clip frame 2 of the looping grip_normal) while its parent keeps its own recorded position, and the pair and the replay diagnostic survive export and reimport.

Without a converted pattern library the saved [5, 6] pair is reported ("the pattern is never guessed") and both captured hand bones hold their incoming pose across a live 0.0667 s step; the pair survives export and reimport.

Headless StudioModel edits and shared Reset to card paths at a fixed clock/camera; production 512x512 renders must change at least 50 pixels by >2/255 and restore exactly (maximum RGBA8 channel delta 0). Check domain isolation, restored export SHA256 against the initial source, and changed-export rejection after reimport. This does not exercise mouse-driven sliders or establish source shader parity.

Headless StudioModel edits and shared Reset to card paths at a fixed clock/camera; production 512x512 renders must change at least 50 pixels by >2/255 and restore exactly (maximum RGBA8 channel delta 0). Check domain isolation, restored export SHA256 against the initial source, and changed-export rejection after reimport. This does not exercise mouse-driven sliders or establish source shader parity.

Headless StudioModel.setSourceOutfit (the Clothes inspector's Outfit picker path) on source character key 65 at a fixed clock/camera: an out-of-range outfit is refused with the document and preview unchanged; outfit 3 must change at least 10,000 pixels of the production 512x512 render by >2/255 and report its unconverted bra slot as conversionMissing; undo, redo and a return to the saved outfit must restore the captured renders exactly (maximum RGBA8 channel delta 0). The saved-outfit export must equal the initial source SHA256 before and after reimport; the outfit-3 export must differ and reimport with Status.coordinateType 3. Outfit 2's converted outer shoes must resolve after reimport. Clothes state, accessory visibility and source shader parity are not covered.
Selects outfit 3 on source character key 65 (render changes at least 10,000 pixels by >2/255) and saves the native document card. The next check loads it in a fresh process.

Loads the document the previous check saved, in a fresh process with NO IKKOKU_SOURCE_SCENE: source character key 65 must rebuild with outfit 3 over its saved outfit 0 (bra slot diagnosed as conversionMissing) while key 0 keeps its saved outfit 0; selecting outfit 0 must change at least 10,000 pixels and undo must restore the loaded render exactly.

ST-C03 import defect control at a fixed clock/camera: source character key 0 saves Status.clothesState 3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3 (all off, shoesType 1) and must import with none of its assembled garments (reference top/bottom, converted outdoor shoes) drawn, while key 65 (all on) draws all three. Forcing key 0's top, bottom and shoes rows on through StudioModel.setSourceClothesState must change at least 10,000 pixels of the production 512x512 render by >2/255; three undos must restore the saved-state render exactly (maximum RGBA8 channel delta 0). Half states, the bra/shorts/socks garments (unconverted, never drawn) and source shader parity are not covered.

Headless StudioModel.setSourceClothesState (the Clothes tab's row path) on source character key 65 at a fixed clock/camera: a state outside 0...3, row 8 and the gloves row (no garment, not a state kind) are refused with document and preview unchanged; top off must change at least 5,000 pixels by >2/255 and leave bottom and shoes drawn; top half on the unconverted (reference) top is drawn dressed with exactly one fallback diagnostic and an unchanged render; undo, redo and a return to on must restore the captured renders exactly (maximum RGBA8 channel delta 0) with no document edit left. The restored export must equal the initial source SHA256 before and after reimport; the top-off export must differ and reimport with Status.clothesState 3,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0 rendering the top-off capture exactly. Native half-state meshes are not converted and not covered.

Headless StudioModel.setSourceAccessoryVisible (the Clothes tab's accessory toggle path) on source character key 10 of the head-200 expansion scene (converted glasses in accessory slot 0, converted top 105-39, bottom 106-25 and shoes 112-1, saved shoesType 0): an empty slot is refused unchanged; hiding slot 0 must change at least 100 pixels by >2/255 (the glasses are small in this framing) and undo/redo restore the captures exactly. The recovered SetClothesState rules run on the converted garments: bottom half advances to off (StateType 1), top half (StateType 0) draws the dressed T-shirt with the n_top_b fallback diagnostic, the shoes row mirrors off to both shoe kinds, the gloves row is refused. The restored export must equal the initial source SHA256 before and after reimport; the slot-0-hidden export must differ and reimport with showAccessory[0] false rendering the hidden capture exactly.
Turns source character key 65's top off (render changes at least 10,000 pixels by >2/255) and key 0's top on, and saves the native document card. The next check loads it in a fresh process.

Loads the document the previous check saved, in a fresh process with NO IKKOKU_SOURCE_SCENE: key 65 must render with its top off (clothes state 3,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,0 over saved all-on) and key 0 with only its top on (0,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3 over saved all-off); turning key 65's top back on must change at least 5,000 pixels and undo must restore the loaded render exactly.

R4 (#115, #110) native IK through the Pose tab's own methods (StudioModel.addCharacter, enableIK, setIKTarget), read from the rendered instance (currentPose, ikFailures): a native female's Left hand IK reaches its target within 1 mm; a +0.02 then -0.02 Stepper round trip on X reproduces the solved arm within 1e-6 (quaternion components and joint metres; the Float32 round trip may move the target by one ulp), while the +0.02 pose is rejected against it; X = 1e20 leaves the chain unsolved with the status 'Left hand IK left unsolved: ' and the arm at its pre-IK pose within 1e-6; X = 0.3 solves again within 1 mm and the status line reads 'Left hand IK solved again.' with no unsolved message. Saves the native document card; the next check loads it. After the save, both hands at X = 1e20 are named in one status line, the left hand's recovery narrows it to the right hand, a later 'Added Kai' status survives an unchanged failure and the right hand's recovery, and no unsolved message remains.

Loads the document the previous check saved, in a fresh process with NO IKKOKU_SOURCE_SCENE: the native female's Left hand IK is on with target X 0.3 and solves to within 1 mm of it, with no unsolved status; turning IK off leaves the hand away from the target (rejected within 1 mm) and undo restores the reach.

Authored clothed bottom-4 fixture: exact selected schema-2 components; scripted live ticks move skirt bone 222 and rendered pixels; FK group 6 and garment-off controls keep the bone within 1e-5 world units. Re-enable, non-skirt outfit switch and native save/load restore motion. Pixel change includes hair motion; the skirt-bone control isolates the garment simulation. Fresh-process native document load restores selected schema-2 skirt bindings and verifies live motion of skirt bone 222 beyond 1e-5 world units after scripted ticks. The preceding reload-save-skirt-dynamics check creates the file.

R7 phase 2, item 3: on the 7-character scenario scene, each editDuringAdvance step starts the live step the way the timer does (off the main thread; a serial step fails the op), lands an edit through the app's own method while the step is in flight (none, move key 65 by 0.25 m in x, FK bone 19 of key 65 to [0,35,0], undo, redo), then completes the step as its completion handler does. Each must advance the clock by exactly one 1/30 s step, present a 512x512 render byte-identical to a full main-thread rebuild of the same document at the same clock, and reuse exactly the step frames the contract allows: all of them without an edit, all but the moved character's after the document-only move, none after an edit that reached a preview (FK, undo, redo). The fk asserts read the edited document; after export and reimport only the character's presence is asserted, since the round trip is not what this check covers. The interleaving inside one step (which worker finishes first) is not controlled; the Engine's sourceStudioEditDuringAParallelTickMatchesTheSerialOrder compares the parallel and serial call orders bit for bit.
